target: Hon skulle vilja resa mer.
english: She would like to travel more.
tip: "Skulle vilja" = would like to. The polite way to express wishes.

target: Jag skulle inte ha gjort det.
english: I wouldn't have done that.
tip: "Skulle inte ha" + supine = wouldn't have. Conditional perfect.

target: Vi lyckas alltid i slutändan.
english: We always succeed in the end.
tip: "Lyckas" (succeed) is deponent. "I slutändan" = in the end.

target: Dessförinnan hade vi ätit middag.
english: Before that we had eaten dinner.
tip: "Dessförinnan" = before that. Formal connector.

target: Han ska plugga till läkare.
english: He's going to study to be a doctor.
tip: "Plugga" = study (informal). "Plugga till" = study to become.

target: Det ryktas att de ska skiljas.
english: It's rumored they're getting divorced.
tip: "Ryktas" = be rumored. Deponent verb.

target: Jag ska lära mig att laga husmanskost.
english: I'm going to learn to cook Swedish home cooking.
tip: "Husmanskost" is traditional Swedish home cooking – hearty, comforting dishes.

target: De slåss om sista platsen.
english: They fight for the last spot.
tip: "Slåss" = to fight. Deponent verb with active meaning.

target: Däremot gillar jag kaffe.
english: On the other hand, I like coffee.
tip: "Däremot" = on the other hand / by contrast.

target: Det kommer att bli bättre.
english: It will get better.
tip: "Kommer att bli" = will become/get. "Bli" is the go-to verb for changes of state.

target: Vi skulle ha stannat längre.
english: We should have stayed longer.
tip: "Skulle ha" + supine also = should have (in hindsight).

target: Vi ska fixa det här.
english: We're going to fix this.
tip: "Fixa" is informal but very common: fixa mat (make food), fixa biljetter (get tickets).

target: Det kommer att regna ikväll.
english: It is going to rain tonight.
tip: "Kommer att" + infinitive expresses predictions, especially weather and external events.

target: Snarare tycker jag det är intressant.
english: Rather, I think it's interesting.
tip: "Snarare" = rather/more accurately.

target: Vi ska gifta oss i sommar.
english: We are getting married this summer.
tip: "Ska" for planned future events. "I sommar" means this/next summer.

target: Jag hade blivit glad om du kunde.
english: I would be happy if you could.
tip: Casual conditional request.

target: Vi ska se till att allt blir klart.
english: We're going to make sure everything is ready.
tip: "Ska" + se till att = going to make sure that.

target: I synnerhet uppskattar jag ärligheten.
english: In particular I appreciate the honesty.
tip: "I synnerhet" = in particular / especially. Formal connector.

target: De ska flytta till Malmö.
english: They are going to move to Malmö.
tip: "Ska" for future plans someone has decided on. "Malmö" is Sweden's third-largest city.

target: En utmanande uppgift på morgonen med vänner.
english: A challenging task in the morning with friends.
tip: "Utmanande" = challenging. From "utmana" (challenge).

target: Strömmen flöt sakta genom den sovande byn.
english: The stream flowed slowly through the sleeping village.
tip: "Sovande" = sleeping (present participle). Personification of the village.

target: Följaktligen ändrade vi planen väldigt ofta förra året.
english: Consequently, we changed the plan very often last year.
tip: "Följaktligen" = consequently/therefore. Formal.

target: Det tog ett tag för mig att vänja mig vid de kalla svenska vintrarna.
english: It took me a while to get used to the cold Swedish winters.
tip: "Tappa sugen" = lose one's enthusiasm/drive.

target: De springande barnen skrattade.
english: The running children laughed.
tip: Participles don't inflect: springande works with any gender/number.

target: Hej då, vi ses senare!
english: Goodbye, see you later!
tip: "Hej" is informal, "God dag" is more formal.

target: Det sjungande barnet var glatt.
english: The singing child was happy.
tip: Present participle as adjective: sjungande (singing). Same form for en/ett/plural.

target: Så länge du är här är jag glad.
english: As long as you're here I'm happy.
tip: "Så länge" = as long as. Second clause inverts after fronted subclause.

target: Jag sprang ut ur huset för att jag insåg att bussen skulle gå.
english: I ran out of the house because I realised the bus was about to leave.
tip: "Älskade" can mean both "beloved" (participle adjective) and "loved" (past tense). Context decides.

target: Allt eftersom tiden gick blev det bättre.
english: As time went on it got better.
tip: "Allt eftersom" = as (gradually over time).

target: De berättade att allt hade gått bra.
english: They told that everything had gone well.
tip: Past perfect in reported speech indicates action before the saying.

target: Hon berättade glatt att hon äntligen hade fått det nya jobbet.
english: She happily told that she had finally gotten the new job.
tip: Reported speech uses past perfect (hade fått) when the original was past tense (fick).

target: Den stängda dörren hela tiden under sommaren.
english: The closed door all the time during summer.
tip: Past participle as adjective: changes for gender! En-word: -d. Ett-word: -t. Plural: -da.

target: Tystnaden var nästan öronbedövande.
english: The silence was almost deafening.
tip: "Öronbedövande" = ear-deafening. Swedish builds vivid compounds: noun + participle.

target: Vi har just kommit hem.
english: We have just come home.
tip: "Just" = just (now). Placed before the supine.

target: Jag ringer upp dig senare.
english: I'll call you back later.
tip: Particle verbs: verb + particle (upp, ner, ut, in, av, på). The particle changes the meaning.

target: Snälla, ta med dig en varm jacka för det är kallt.
english: Please, bring a warm jacket because it is cold.
tip: Swedish particle verbs: the particle (upp, ut, in, av, på) often completely changes the verb's meaning.

target: De anställda på företaget.
english: The employees at the company.
tip: "Anställd" (employed) functions as both participle and noun.

target: Kundservicen på den där butiken är under all kritik.
english: The customer service at that shop is beneath contempt.
tip: Means so bad it can't even be criticized properly.

target: Jag är otroligt stolt över vad vi har åstadkommit tillsammans i år.
english: I am incredibly proud of what we have accomplished together this year.
tip: Present participle is invariable – same form for en/ett/plural: "en/ett/de växande..."

target: Hon har just blivit befordrad till avdelningschef efter fem års engagerat arbete.
english: She has just been promoted to head of department after five years of dedicated work.
tip: Past participle as adj agrees with gender: parkerad (en), parkerat (ett), parkerade (pl/def).

target: Jag är så stolt över min son som vann den regionala naturvetenskapstävlingen förra veckan.
english: I am so proud of my son for winning the regional science competition last week.
tip: Strong verb past participle: skriven (en), skrivet (ett), skrivna (plural).

target: Det sägs att sommaren blir varm.
english: It's said the summer will be warm.
tip: "Det sägs att" = it is said that – impersonal reported speech.

target: Förlåt att jag är sen efter jobbet!
english: Sorry I'm late after work!
tip: Casual apology among friends.

target: Han sa att han inte hade hunnit.
english: He said he hadn't had time.
tip: In subordinate clause: "att han inte hade hunnit" – inte before verb.

target: Ursäkta att jag stör, men jag behöver fråga dig om rapporten.
english: Excuse me for interrupting, but I need to ask you about the report.
tip: Formal/polite opener before asking a stranger something.

target: Han tog skeden i vacker hand.
english: He tackled the task gracefully.
tip: To accept a difficult situation and deal with it.

target: Ärade åhörare, jag vill tacka er alla för att ni kom.
english: Dear listeners, I want to thank you all for coming.
tip: Very formal opening for speeches.

target: Det är med stor glädje jag meddelar.
english: It is with great pleasure that I announce this.
tip: Very formal announcement style.

target: Tack så hjärtligt för er hjälp med att ordna evenemanget.
english: Thank you most kindly for your help with organising the event.
tip: Very formal thanks. Rarely used in everyday speech.

target: Var god och fyll i formuläret.
english: Please fill in the form.
tip: "Var god" = please. Standard in official instructions.

target: Att lägga locket på.
english: To put a lid on it.
tip: Means to stop discussing something, to sweep it under the carpet.

target: Det finns 365 dagar på ett år.
english: There are 365 days in a year.
tip: "På" used idiomatically: "dagar på ett år" = days in a year.

target: Det kliar i fingrarna sedan länge här.
english: My fingers have been itching for a while now.
tip: Means eager to do something.

target: Oasen erbjöd skugga och vatten mitt i öknen.
english: The oasis offered shade and water in the middle of the desert.
tip: The familiarity and directness of Swedish informal register – "du" with everyone.

target: Trubaduren sjöng medeltida ballader vid slottet.
english: The troubadour sang medieval ballads at the castle.
tip: "Det är DU som bestämmer" emphasizes who. Very common pattern.

target: Jag vore ytterst tacksam i affären.
english: I would be most grateful in business.
tip: "Vore" is subjunctive – extremely polite. Formal letters/requests.

target: Tack, det var snällt under veckan redan!
english: Thanks, that was kind during the week already!
tip: Casual and warm.

target: Det åligger var och en att följa reglerna.
english: It is incumbent upon everyone to follow the rules.
tip: "Åligger" = it is the duty of. Very formal/legal.

target: Det är soft hela tiden.
english: It's laid-back all the time.
tip: "Soft" (from English) is slang for easy, relaxed, cool.

target: Vi ber att få återkomma.
english: We ask to return to this matter.
tip: Formal customer service language.
